  First, a correction to how I put this earlier. I said we were losing money on it. Per token that's true, but I checked the actual traffic and the model as a whole is not losing money, so don't decide this as if moneyispouringout.

  What's actually true: the output row of its price card is under cost. Output costs us $0.55 per million tokens and we charge $0.20 — about

  fix(director,gateway): seed delivery hardening for restore + all PrePrompt sends (#212)

  Three root-cause fixes the restore E2E forced out of hiding; the first
  applies to every PrePrompt/handover seed, not just restore:

  1. PrePrompt readiness gate (ControlEndpoints): ActivityState reads
     WaitingForInput from t=0, so seeds were dispatched into a BOOTING
     claude - typed text reached the composer, Enter keypresses were
     dropped, the prompt parked unsubmitted. Now waits for the startup
     burst to render and the TUI to settle before dispatching.

  2. @-reference submit watchdog (AtReferenceSubmitVerifier, both PTY
     backends): claude's path-autocomplete can eat the submitting Enter.
     The watchdog judges by output rhythm - dead window -> nudge, settling
     window -> wait, streaming -> done. Screen-parsing and one-shot growth
     checks were tried and defeated live; the class doc records why.

  3. Restore spawn timeout (GatewayEndpoints): the shared 2s Director
     client timed out on claude.exe spawns, leaving orphan sessions
     (created, never renamed or journal-cleaned). Dedicated 20s client,
     same as the cross-director handover's spawn leg.

  Live-proven restoring 4 real sessions lost to an abrupt Director kill:
  every seed passed the gate, and the watchdog recovered two genuinely
  eaten Enters ("submitted after 1 nudge(s)"). 5 new watchdog tests.

  fix(director,gateway): seed delivery hardening for restore + all PrePrompt sends (#212)

  Three root-cause fixes the restore E2E forced out of hiding; the first
  applies to every PrePrompt/handover seed, not just restore:

  1. PrePrompt readiness gate (ControlEndpoints): ActivityState reads
     WaitingForInput from t=0, so seeds were dispatched into a BOOTING
     claude - typed text reached the composer, Enter keypresses were
     dropped, the prompt parked unsubmitted. Now waits for the startup
     burst to render and the TUI to settle before dispatching.

  2. @-reference submit watchdog (AtReferenceSubmitVerifier, both PTY
     backends): claude's path-autocomplete can eat the submitting Enter.
     The watchdog judges by output rhythm - dead window -> nudge, settling
     window -> wait, streaming -> done. Screen-parsing and one-shot growth
     checks were tried and defeated live; the class doc records why.

  3. Restore spawn timeout (GatewayEndpoints): the shared 2s Director
     client timed out on claude.exe spawns, leaving orphan sessions
     (created, never renamed or journal-cleaned). Dedicated 20s client,
     same as the cross-director handover's spawn leg.

  Live-proven restoring 4 real sessions lost to an abrupt Director kill:
  every seed passed the gate, and the watchdog recovered two genuinely
  eaten Enters ("submitted after 1 nudge(s)"). 5 new watchdog tests.

  fix(director,gateway): seed delivery hardening for restore + all PrePrompt sends (#212)

  applies to every PrePrompt/handover seed, not just restore:

  1. PrePrompt readiness gate (ControlEndpoints): ActivityState reads
     WaitingForInput from t=0, so seeds were dispatched into a BOOTING
     claude - typed text reached the composer, Enter keypresses were
     dropped, the prompt parked unsubmitted. Now waits for the startup
     burst to render and the TUI to settle before dispatching.

  2. @-reference submit watchdog (AtReferenceSubmitVerifier, both PTY
     backends): claude's path-autocomplete can eat the submitting Enter.
     The watchdog judges by output rhythm - dead window -> nudge, settling
     window -> wait, streaming -> done. Screen-parsing and one-shot growth
     checks were tried and defeated live; the class doc records why.

  3. Restore spawn timeout (GatewayEndpoints): the shared 2s Director
     client timed out on claude.exe spawns, leaving orphan sessions
     (created, never renamed or journal-cleaned). Dedicated 20s client,
     same as the cross-director handover's spawn leg.

  Live-proven restoring 4 real sessions lost to an abrupt Director kill:
  every seed passed the gate, and the watchdog recovered two genuinely
  eaten Enters ("submitted after 1 nudge(s)"). 5 new watchdog tests.

  fix(director,gateway): seed delivery hardening for restore + all PrePrompt sends (#212)

  applies to every PrePrompt/handover seed, not just restore:

     claude - typed text reached the composer, Enter keypresses were
     dropped, the prompt parked unsubmitted. Now waits for the startup
     burst to render and the TUI to settle before dispatching.

  2. @-reference submit watchdog (AtReferenceSubmitVerifier, both PTY
     backends): claude's path-autocomplete can eat the submitting Enter.
     The watchdog judges by output rhythm - dead window -> nudge, settling
     window -> wait, streaming -> done. Screen-parsing and one-shot growth
     checks were tried and defeated live; the class doc records why.

  3. Restore spawn timeout (GatewayEndpoints): the shared 2s Director
     client timed out on claude.exe spawns, leaving orphan sessions
     (created, never renamed or journal-cleaned). Dedicated 20s client,
     same as the cross-director handover's spawn leg.

  Live-proven restoring 4 real sessions lost to an abrupt Director kill:
  every seed passed the gate, and the watchdog recovered two genuinely
  eaten Enters ("submitted after 1 nudge(s)"). 5 new watchdog tests.

  The three worth thinking about alongside DevTiller:

  devrudder — the rudder is what the tiller actually steers. More people know "rudder" than "tiller." Same nautical family, slightly more
  recognisable.

  devbearing — "get your bearings" is an everyday phrase. Means knowing where you are and where you're headed. That maps well to what the product
  does for a developer with many agents running.

  devthrottle — caution here: in tech, "throttling" usually means limiting something (rate limiting, CPU throttling). Could read as the thing that
  slows your agents down rather than the thing that controls them.
